title: Copy-Protection with Correlated Challenges: Point Functions and More via Decisional Coset Monogamy
authors: Amit Behera, Alper Çakan, Vipul Goyal
abstract: Copy-protection encodes a functionality in a reusable quantum state that cannot be split into two states (freeloader adversaries) which remain simultaneously useful. Prior plain-model results handle only independently sampled challenges; the more natural identical-challenge notion, also tied to unclonable bits and copy-protection of point functions, has remained open. We strengthen these definitions and prove plain-model security for our new stronger notions. For single-decryptor encryption (SDE) we define correlated challenge security, show it implies all previous SDE notions including identical-challenge security, and prove that the construction of Kitagawa and Yamakawa (TCC'25) achieves it assuming iO and one-way functions. We also nearly fully characterize the relations among prior SDE notions. For general functionalities we define correlated challenge unclonable puncturable obfuscation (UPO), allowing arbitrary correlations among challenge points and puncturing bits plus auxiliary information before and after splitting, and requiring only conditionally uniform bits and $λ^c$ average conditional min-entropy in each point separately (thus, in particular, the points may be identical). Assuming post-quantum iO and quantum-hard LWE, we construct correlated UPO for polynomial-size keyed circuits with input length at least $λ^c$, answering an open question of Ananth, Behera, Huang, Kitagawa, Yamakawa (EUROCRYPT'26) and of Cakan-Goyal (EUROCRYPT'26). We also obtain the first plain-model copy protection for point functions, $k$-point functions, and compute-and-compare programs, and identical-challenge copy protection for general puncturable functionalities.
summary: This paper advances the theory of quantum cryptography by developing robust security notions for copy-protection and encryption that account for correlated or identical challenges. It provides constructions proving the existence of these secure primitives for general functionalities, resolving long-standing open questions in the field.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical challenge of defining and proving security for quantum copy-protection and single-decryptor encryption (SDE) under natural, correlated challenge distributions, moving beyond simple independent challenges.
main_result: The authors establish plain-model security for correlated challenge unclonable puncturable obfuscation (UPO) and achieve the first provable identical-challenge copy protection for point functions and general puncturable functionalities.
method: The methodology involves strengthening security definitions (e.g., correlated challenge security) and utilizing advanced cryptographic techniques, including a new decisional monogamy theorem for coset states, and relying on assumptions like post-quantum iO and quantum-hard LWE.
model_or_system: The work is purely theoretical, dealing with abstract cryptographic primitives applied to quantum states and computational circuits. The model involves quantum states, challenge samplers, and polynomial-size keyed circuits ($	ext{Circ}$).
key_observables: Security notions such as correlated challenge security, identical-challenge security, and the success probability of distinguishing real vs. simulated quantum states.
important_parameters: Security parameter $\lambda$, and the min-entropy $	ext{eH}_\infty(D\lambda)$ of the challenge sampler.
main_assumptions: The results assume the existence of post-quantum indistinguishability obfuscation (iO), one-way functions, and the quantum hardness of LWE.
figures_summary: Not specified (The notes refer to general concepts and theorems rather than specific figure contents).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining stronger security notions for SDE and UPO to handle correlations, then proving the existence of constructions satisfying these notions using advanced cryptographic machinery, and finally applying these results to specific functions like point functions.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, the rigorous mathematical framework developed for handling correlations in quantum information security has parallels with understanding complex, non-independent interactions in many-body quantum systems, where local measurements might reveal global correlations.
